name: latin-phrases

title.en: Latin phrases in English and Swedish
title.sv: Latinska uttryck i svenskan och engelskan

description.en: 77 Latin phrases still used in both English and Swedish, from ad hoc and carpe diem to status quo and vice versa. The Latin phrase on the front, its meaning in English and Swedish on the back, with the literal sense or origin as a note where it helps. Every phrase has an entry in Dictionary.com and in a Swedish reference work (Svenska Akademiens ordlista, Svensk ordbok or Nationalencyklopedin) and is recorded in Wikidata; the meanings are written for this deck, using the conventional translation where a phrase has one, and checked against those dictionaries and Wiktionary.
description.sv: 77 latinska uttryck som fortfarande används både på svenska och engelska, från ad hoc och carpe diem till status quo och vice versa. Det latinska uttrycket på framsidan, betydelsen på svenska och engelska på baksidan, med den ordagranna betydelsen eller ursprunget som anteckning där det hjälper. Varje uttryck finns i Dictionary.com och i ett svenskt uppslagsverk (Svenska Akademiens ordlista, Svensk ordbok eller Nationalencyklopedin) och är registrerat i Wikidata; betydelserna är skrivna för den här kortleken, med den vedertagna översättningen där uttrycket har en, och kontrollerade mot de ordböckerna och Wiktionary.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Candidates. The authoring agent wrote a list of Latin phrases it judged to be in current English or Swedish use, from its own general knowledge; with duplicates and single words removed it holds 216 multi-word phrases. No list was copied from any source.

Swedish use. Each candidate was looked up in SAOL and Svensk ordbok through the svenska.se search API (https://svenska.se/api/search/saol and /api/search/so, parameters q, size=10, exactMatch=true), searching for the whole phrase and for each of its words longer than two letters, and keeping a hit when the phrase is the headword (field ortografi) or an idiom (field idiom) of a returned article. Each candidate was also looked up in Nationalencyklopedin at https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<phrase with spaces as hyphens>, keeping a hit when the page has an article title (reader-title heading); the title and opening text were saved. A missing NE article means only that no page exists at that URL slug: NE returns the same error page for a slug that does not exist at all as for a phrase it may treat under another title, so a “no” from NE is not proof that NE never mentions the phrase.

English use. Each candidate was looked up at https://www.dictionary.com/browse/<phrase with spaces as hyphens> without following redirects: HTTP 200 means the phrase has its own entry (its meta description, which carries the first definition, was saved); a 301 redirect to another word or a 404 means it has none. Merriam-Webster, Cambridge and Collins refused automated requests (HTTP 403), so Dictionary.com is the English dictionary of record.

Wikidata. Each candidate was searched with the Wikidata API (wbsearchentities, type item and type lexeme, languages la, en and sv) and the matching entities fetched with wbgetentities (labels, aliases, descriptions, claims, lemmas, senses). For each card the item that represents the phrase itself was chosen by hand (for example Q190273 for carpe diem rather than artworks named after it); where no such item exists, English or Swedish lexemes with the phrase as lemma serve instead.
Wiktionary. The English and Swedish Wiktionary wikitext of each candidate was fetched with action=raw and its definition lines kept, for checking meanings only.

Other avenues tried and not used: a first SAOL/SO pass searched only the whole phrase and missed idioms filed under one of their words (for example per capita under capita in SO), so the word-by-word search above replaced it; a Wikidata SPARQL query for lexemes timed out (HTTP 504), so the API search was used instead; Folkets lexikon (the KTH Swedish–English dictionary, CC BY-SA 2.5) was downloaded as XML from https://folkets-lexikon.csc.kth.se/folkets/folkets_sv_en_public.xml and matched only four of the first 134 candidates (ad notam, alter ego, nota bene, vice versa), too few to serve as a usage criterion; frequency counts in Språkbanken’s Korp news corpora (API https://ws.spraakbanken.gu.se/ws/korp/v8/, corpus list from /info) were too small and noisy (names of series and bands) to serve as one either. The Korp count requests themselves were not recorded verbatim when they were run, so they are not listed under Queries; the URLs that were recorded are. None of these avenues contributed anything to the deck.

Selection. A candidate was kept if it has an entry in Dictionary.com and in at least one of SAOL, Svensk ordbok or NE, then the exclusions listed under Selection were applied (non-Latin phrases, names and titles, a disputed subject, senses that differ between the languages, no Wikidata entity).

Writing the cards. Front: the phrase in Latin as Dictionary.com, SAOL, SO and NE spell it (lower case, j in de jure, ipso jure and res judicata, capital D in anno Domini, the commas of cogito, ergo sum and veni, vidi, vici). Back: a short meaning in English and in Swedish. Where a phrase has an established, conventional translation or fixed Swedish equivalent — a fact of the language that every dictionary repeats, such as “I came, I saw, I conquered”, “skynda långsamt” or “å ämbetets vägnar” — the back uses it; otherwise the meaning is the authoring agent’s own wording, and no dictionary definition or explanatory wording was copied (backs that had come too close to a definition were reworded in quality-control rounds 1 and 3). Where a phrase has a narrower sense in one language the back gives the sense common to both. A back note gives the literal sense, the origin (author, motto, field), an abbreviation or the contrasting phrase when it helps; every fact in a note is stated by at least one of NE, Dictionary.com, Wiktionary, SAOL, SO or Wikidata in the card’s evidence.

Cross-checking. Every card’s meaning was compared with the definitions saved from the Swedish source(s), Dictionary.com and Wiktionary; the evidence of each card quotes what those sources returned on 2026-10-04 (generated from the saved responses, trimmed). Wikidata label checks were added wherever the front, or a back text, is exactly (same case and punctuation) a Wikidata label or alias of the chosen item in that language (when only the multilingual “mul” label matches, one check is written for Latin, which the builder compares with mul labels too); they are run against live Wikidata by authored_decks.py check/build. After the review rounds, every back and note was compared mechanically with every quoted source text of its card (any segment of three or more words between commas or semicolons, and any whole back; before comparing, case and punctuation are normalised, parenthesised abbreviations such as “(a.m.)” or “(RIP)” are removed, a leading article is ignored and “/” in a source is read as “or”/“eller”). The first run (round 3) compared whole backs including the parenthesis and only backs of two or more words, and so missed six cards; the corrected run (round 4) flags only the conventional translations listed under Licensing. The quotations in the evidence were shortened to what confirms the card (gloss, literal sense, origin), with omissions marked “…” and NE’s pronunciation keys replaced by “[…]”.
selection: The deck holds the multi-word Latin phrases, from a candidate list of 216, that have their own entry in Dictionary.com (English) and appear in at least one Swedish reference work — as a headword or idiom in Svenska Akademiens ordlista or Svensk ordbok, or as a Nationalencyklopedin article — and that Wikidata records as an item or lexeme. 91 candidates met the dictionary criteria; 14 were then left out: “a cappella”: Italian, not Latin (NE: “italienska, egentligen ’i kapellstil’”). “lingua franca”: Italian, not Latin (NE: “italienska, egentligen ’frankernas språk’”). “homo sapiens”: a scientific species name, not a phrase of general use. “agnus dei”: a liturgical text and title (NE: a litany sung at the breaking of bread). “dies irae”: the title of a hymn of the requiem mass. “de profundis”: NE treats it as the Latin title of Psalm 130. “dominus vobiscum”: a liturgical greeting rather than a phrase used in everyday English or Swedish. “opus dei”: the NE article is about the Catholic organisation of that name. “pax romana”: the name of a historical period, not a phrase used of anything else. “pro patria”: the NE article is about the Swedish charitable society Pro Patria, not the phrase, so the Swedish criterion is not really met. “in corpore”: the Swedish sense (SAOL, SO: “med fulltalig representation”, as a whole body) differs from the English one (Dictionary.com: “in body; in substance”), so one back would mislead one of the two audiences. “jus primae noctis”: it names an alleged right whose historical existence is disputed (NE: “… förekommit i Europa är omstridd”). “ecce homo”: Wikidata has no item or lexeme for the phrase itself (only artworks titled so), so the card would have no CC0 content source. “terra firma”: Wikidata has no item or lexeme for the phrase (only unrelated works and the general item “land”), so the card would have no CC0 content source. Single Latin words (veto, alibi, ergo) and abbreviations (e.g., i.e., etc.) are outside the deck. Phrases that did not meet the criteria include several well-known ones (alea iacta est, et cetera, per se, quid pro quo, sui generis, vox populi, habeas corpus): either Dictionary.com has no entry for them or none of SAOL, SO and NE had a matching headword, idiom or article at the URL tried; they can be added if a later check finds them. rounds.summary: Every card’s meaning was compared with Dictionary.com, the Swedish source(s) found and, where they have an entry, English and Swedish Wiktionary; 81 Wikidata label checks were written and pass. Discrepancies between sources were resolved as recorded in the findings; candidates that failed a criterion or had a problem were excluded rather than forced in.

findings.issue: Wiktionary calls “seize the day” a common mistranslation (it gives “enjoy the day”, “make the most of today”); NE glosses it ’njut dagen’, Dictionary.com “seize the day; enjoy the present”.
findings.resolution: Back gives the established rendering and the sense: “seize the day; make the most of today” / “fånga dagen; ta vara på dagen”, with the literal “pluck the day” in the note.

findings.issue: Dictionary.com’s first sense is “manner of living; way of life”; SAOL, SO, NE and Wiktionary give the provisional working arrangement between parties who disagree, which is the current sense in both languages.
findings.resolution: Back gives the arrangement sense; the literal “way of living” is in the note.

findings.issue: SAOL defines it as “oprövad person, metod e.d.”, SO as “oskrivet blad”; Dictionary.com as “a mind not yet affected by experiences”.
findings.resolution: Back “a blank slate” / “ett oskrivet blad” covers the common figurative sense.

findings.issue: Wikidata item Q209896 is “honorary degree”, not the phrase; its Swedish label is “honoris causa”.

findings.issue: Wikidata has no item for the adverbial phrase; Q155736 “good faith” has the Swedish alias “bona fide” and Latin label “bona fides”.
findings.resolution: Q155736 used, with a Swedish alias check on “bona fide”.

findings.issue: Wikidata’s Swedish alias is “så förgås världens härlighet”; NE has “så förgår världens härlighet”.
findings.resolution: Back follows NE (“förgår”, the usual present tense of förgå); no Swedish label check was written for the back.

A mechanical overlap check of every back and note against every quoted “says” of its card was then run (see Queries): it also caught memento-mori en (“remember that you must die”, now “remember that you will die”), pro-forma en (“as a matter of form”, now “for form’s sake”) and in-extenso sv (“i sin helhet; oförkortat”, now “i full längd; utan strykningar”).
